customer_acme: Hey team — we're seeing tool calls fail intermittently when uploading a small PDF via the browser TS SDK. Error from your endpoint: `json: invalid UTF-8 in string` and the tool runtime rejects the call. Started after upgrading to 1.12.0. (high impact, production)

mike_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the request payload (or first ~200 bytes) and SDK version? Also sending logs/traces helps.

customer_acme: SDK v1.12.0 (cdn build). Here's the first 64 bytes we captured from the request body (hex): `ff fe 25 00 50 00 44 00 46 00 2d 00 31 00 2e 00 0a 00 ...` — looks like a UTF-16LE BOM? The server shows: `tool-runtime: schema validation failed: invalid character '�' in string literal`

jia_engineer: That hex definitely looks like a UTF-16LE encoded string (FF FE = BOM). Our Go unmarshal expects UTF-8 JSON strings, so any 0x00 bytes will break parsing. Do you have a minimal repro (TS snippet) you can share?

customer_acme: Minimal repro from browser:
```ts
const file = await fetch('/file.pdf').then(r => r.arrayBuffer());
const u16 = new Uint16Array(file);
const payload = { doc: String.fromCharCode.apply(null, u16) };
await RedwoodClient.callTool('pdf-extract', payload);
```
This used to work in older SDK build we had.

ashley_sdk: Ah I think I see what's happening. The snippet converts the raw bytes into a UTF-16 string (Uint16Array -> String.fromCharCode) and then the SDK serializes that into JSON as-is. Because those bytes contain 0x00 for each high/low pair, Go's JSON parser sees NULs and invalid UTF-8 sequences. Older builds may have coerced via base64; v1.12.0 added a micro-optim that tried to convert ArrayBuffer->string to reduce size, and it guessed UTF-16 for some transfers.

mike_support: Can you confirm whether the SDK attempted a `TextDecoder('utf-16le')` conversion, or if this is purely from the app code above? Also what headers are being set for the tool arg? e.g., `encoding: 'utf-8'` or `binary: true`?

customer_acme: No explicit header. We only pass a JS object with `doc: <string>` so SDK handles serialization. We didn't expect the SDK to flip encoding.

jia_engineer: Repro on our side: ran that TS snippet, appended payload into the JSON body. Go rejects during json.Unmarshal with: `invalid UTF-8` and logs the first bytes contain 0x00. Quick raw capture: `{"doc":"\u0000P\u0000D\u0000F\u0000-\u00001\u0000\n\u0000"}` — so the PDF bytes show up as UTF-16 code units escaped as NUL-prefixed characters.

lee_sre: Deploy-bot shows that a canary of SDK v1.12.0 rolled yesterday with a change to arraybuffer->string handling (PR #6789). Rolling back that micro-opt seems safe until we ship a proper fix. @ashley_sdk can you confirm?

deploy-bot: canary rollout of redwood-js-sdk@1.12.0 started 2026-03-15T09:02:01Z -> 15% traffic

ashley_sdk: Confirmed. PR #6789 added a heuristic to avoid base64 bloat by trying to interpret binary as UTF-8/UTF-16 text and send as JSON strings. That heuristic mis-detects binary PDFs as UTF-16LE in some browser builds. Immediate mitigations:
- App-side: stop converting raw bytes to JS string; instead send base64. Example workaround: `const b64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(file))); api.callTool({ doc_b64: b64, _encoding: 'base64' })`.
- SDK-side hotfix: we can revert the heuristic (fast) or force base64 for any ArrayBuffer/TypedArray when the bytes contain 0x00 in odd positions (heuristic). Plan: revert canary and publish 1.12.1 within the hour.

mike_support: Customer impact = API errors for tool calls resulting in failed user flows. Any billing/latency fallout?

lee_sre: We saw ~120 failed tool calls across 3 customers correlated with 1.12.0 canary window. No significant cost spike but user-facing errors.

customer_acme: Workaround implemented on our side (base64 path). Confirming it stops the errors. Thanks.

jia_engineer: For the engineer triage: steps to reproduce + logs we have:
1) Browser TS: fetch arrayBuffer -> Uint16Array -> String.fromCharCode -> pass as arg.
2) Redwood JS SDK serializes object -> JSON body contains NULs / UTF-16 surrogate escapes.
3) Go API attempts json.Unmarshal -> fails with invalid UTF-8.

Attach sample debug payload (first 120 bytes base64): `//UE...` (sent to internal bug ticket).

ashley_sdk: Next actions:
- Revert canary micro-opt and push 1.12.1 (hotfix) -> ETA 45m.
- Add robust rule: never emit raw binary as plain JSON strings. Always base64-encode typed arrays unless explicitly annotated `text/utf-8`.
- Add unit tests for PDFs/PNGs/MP3s and for edge cases where bytes look like UTF-16 BOM.

mike_support: I'll mark this thread P1->eng oncall and notify affected customers. Customer says workaround works, but they want a fix in SDK.

customer_acme: Appreciated. We'll keep the workaround for now. Please ping when 1.12.1 is published so we can upgrade. :thumbsup: 

lee_sre: rolling back canary now. deploy-bot: trigger rollback job.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for redwood-js-sdk@1.12.0 -> version 1.11.9 restored to 100% traffic

ashley_sdk: Patch PR ready (revert + tests). Will cut 1.12.1 after CI passes. Expect release notes: "Fix: avoid UTF-16 mis-detect for typed arrays; always base64 binary tool args"

mike_support: Closing loop: customer confirmed fix after SDK update? please update thread when verified.

customer_acme: I'll test the new SDK and post results here once upgraded. Thanks all. :pray:
